_comment: The pinned watch list for the regression gate (C-004). Every bot that has ever shown a
divergence stays here, including ones whose cause was found and fixed -- a defect removed
from the watch list is a defect free to return unnoticed.
Note that every baseline_delta_pct is null, and that is the point. The observed_delta_pct
figures below were measured at ten rounds in a setup matching no division exactly, and
before both the event-dispatch redesign and the Bot API upgrade that AN-001 and ADR-001
describe. They record why each bot is being watched; they are not something to measure
against, and treating them as baselines would gate on numbers that describe a bridge that
M-006 produces the first real baselines, at official division parameters over averaged
repeats. Until then --regression reports NO BASELINE for these rows rather than a verdict.

bots.note: Scores much lower under the bridge with no errors on either side. AN-005 and AN-006 are the first named candidates to check against.
The largest unexplained drop in the collection, and no errors logged on either side.
Scores lower under the bridge with no errors.
Scores higher under the bridge. A robot that improves is as much a fidelity defect as one that degrades, and is easier to leave unexamined.
Scores higher under the bridge. A bullet-surfing robot depends on precise radar and bullet state, so PHY-005 and PHY-008 are worth checking here.

The bot that surfaced the missing file sandbox: writes root paths and produces access-denied errors in the thousands under the bridge. Expected to resolve at M-004; the fail-fast rule will stop its battle before then.

Was a total failure -- zero score across every round -- caused by the Bot API event queue dropping deferred same-priority events (ADR-001). Fixed and within threshold. Kept on the list so it stays fixed.

Reported, never gated. Its classic-side score swung between 6 and 274 across runs with no bridge involved, so a percentage delta on it is arithmetic rather than measurement (AN-001). The +621.9% inversion once attributed to the bridge disappeared with the event-dispatch redesign.
